curator_note: AI-curated independent gold. Topic: Causal inference for treatment effects in observational data. Corpus era: 2020-2025.

topics.topic: Causal inference methods for estimating treatment effects in observational data
topics.review_note: Papers covering: propensity score methods, instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, double ML, synthetic control.

paper_relevance.title: Causal Inference Using Potential Outcomes: Design, Modeling, Decisions
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Foundational textbook framework for causal inference with potential outcomes — propensity score methods, matching, and weighting for observational data.

paper_relevance.title: Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Treatment and Structural Parameters
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Double ML — debiased estimation of treatment effects using ML nuisance estimation with cross-fitting. Combines propensity score modeling with ML, handles high-dimensional confounders.

paper_relevance.title: Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: R-Learner for CATE estimation — decomposes HTE estimation using propensity scores and outcome regression. Widely used in observational studies.

paper_relevance.title: Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment Timing
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Robust DiD estimator with staggered treatment adoption — addresses heterogeneity bias in two-way FE DiD. Critical for modern DiD-based causal inference.

paper_relevance.title: A Practical Guide to Causal Inference in the Health Sciences Using Observational Data
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Practical guide covering propensity score matching, IPW, IV methods for health sciences observational data. Directly relevant to treatment effect estimation.

paper_relevance.title: Synthetic Difference-in-Differences
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Synthetic DiD — combines synthetic control with DiD for improved causal estimation in observational studies with panel data.

paper_relevance.title: Machine Learning for Causal Inference: A Survey
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Survey of ML methods for causal inference: doubly robust estimators, causal forests, DeepIV, neural IV — covers all expected themes.

paper_relevance.title: Causal Inference: A Statistics and Machine Learning Perspective
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Comprehensive perspective on causal inference from both statistics and ML viewpoints — covers propensity scoring, IV, natural experiments.

paper_relevance.title: Causal Inference with Large Language Models
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: LLM-assisted causal inference — using LLMs for confounder identification, treatment coding, and effect estimation in observational data.

paper_relevance.title: IV Methods for Endogenous Treatment: A Review
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Review of instrumental variable methods for endogenous treatment in observational data — 2SLS, LATE, weak instrument tests. Directly addresses IV theme.

paper_relevance.title: Generalized Random Forests (Causal Forests)
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Causal forests — heterogeneous treatment effect estimation using random forests with honesty. Widely used for CATE estimation in observational studies.

paper_relevance.title: Estimating Treatment Effects with Causal Forests: An Application
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Applied causal forests tutorial with observational data — demonstrates CATE estimation, overlap weighting, and confidence interval construction.

paper_relevance.title: Regression Discontinuity Designs: A Practical Review
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: RDD — exploits threshold-based treatment assignment as quasi-experiment. Local randomization framework. Complementary to IV for causal identification in observational data.

paper_relevance.title: DAGs with NO TEARS: Continuous Optimization for Structure Learning
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: NOTEARS — continuous optimization for learning causal DAGs from observational data. Enables automated confound identification for treatment effect estimation.

paper_relevance.title: LLMs for Causal Reasoning: A Survey of Counterfactual and Interventional Inference
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Survey of LLM capabilities for causal reasoning: counterfactual generation, confounder identification, treatment effect verbalization from observational data.

topics.reference_answer: Estimating treatment effects from observational data requires addressing confounding. Three main methodological families: (1) Propensity score methods: inverse probability weighting, matching, and doubly-robust estimators; Double ML (Chernozhukov et al.) combines ML nuisance estimation with cross-fitting for high-dimensional confounders; R-Learner estimates CATE. (2) Instrumental variables: 2SLS identifies LATE when valid instruments exist; weak instrument problem requires robust inference; DeepIV extends IV to nonparametric settings. (3) Difference-in-differences: parallel trends assumption must hold; modern robust DiD (Callaway & Sant'Anna) handles staggered adoption; Synthetic DiD combines synthetic control with DiD. Key challenge: all methods require strong assumptions (unconfoundedness, valid instrument, parallel trends) that are often untestable.
